newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mining crucial to southern Africa economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Mining crucial to southern Africa economic growth.

text.p: Southern Africa was on the road to considerable economic growth and mining would play a crucial role in the region's revitalisation, Standard Bank Ltd economist Phillip Clayton said on Monday.
Clayton told a mining and metals conference in Johannesburg that inward investment needed to be welcomed with open arms by countries in the region.
"Such a strategy makes it more likely that southern Africa will grow over the next couple of decades and more than reverse the negative legacy of the recent past," Clayton said.
He said mining, already crucial to the region's economy, would grow in importance as new projects came onstream.

"Mining is likely to provide the kick-start required by southern Africa if the region is to grow in a meaningful way that will lead to the upliftment of the majority of the subcontinent's 150 million or so people," he said.

Clayton cited the development of BHP Ltd and Delta Gold NL's joint venture Hartley Platinum mine in Zimbabwe and the pending privatisation of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) as some of the current exciting mining developments in southern Africa.
Clayton said sub-Saharan Africa's exports from 1970 to 1993 grew by a mere 1.8 percent a year compared to east Asia and the Pacific region which saw exports grow by 10 percent every year.
"Economic stagnation and political intolerance meant that Africa exported up to 50,000 skilled workers per year to the developed world.
"The loss in entrepreneurial spirit of these people can only be guessed at," Clayton added.
He listed corruption, AIDS, fears of nationalisation, and lack of infrastructure in large parts of the region as restricting investments.
Clayton said the region needed to sell itself to investors.
"Attitudes towards investment need to be positive, from head of state to the lowliest bureaucrat".
